question_eng: Until what point can Person B exercise their right to claim damages against Person A?
answer_eng: Person B must file a legal claim against Person A within one year from the date the goods were delivered, or the right to claim damages will be extinguished. However, this period may be extended by mutual agreement between Person A and Person B.
background_eng:
Person A entered into a transportation contract with Person B to transport Person B's goods to a specified destination. During the contract formation process, Person B informed Person A in advance that damages could occur if the goods did not arrive on time. However, an issue arose during transportation, resulting in the goods arriving three days later than scheduled, causing damages to Person B.

Person B intended to claim damages for this delay but was unable to file a lawsuit immediately due to a busy schedule. Consequently, Person B is contemplating the deadline by which they must file a lawsuit from the date the goods were delivered.

contexts.content_eng: The claims and obligations of a carrier against a consignor or consignee shall be terminated, whatever the causes for the claims may be, where no judicial claim is made within one year after the date when the carrier has delivered or will deliver the cargo to the consignee: Provided, That this period may be extended by an agreement between the parties.
contexts.index_eng: COMMERCIAL ACT / Article. 814 / Termination of Claims and Obligations of Carriers

question_eng: What punishment could Person A face for secretly entering Person B's house at night and stealing the gold necklace?

question_eng: If Person B determines that there is a significant reason making it difficult to continue the marriage due to Person A's gambling addiction, can Person B file for judicial divorce? Additionally, when does this right to file expire?
answer_eng: According to Article 840 of the Civil Code, Person B may file for divorce if there is a significant reason making it difficult to continue the marriage with Person A. Pursuant to Article 842 of the Civil Code, Person B's right to file for divorce expires 6 months from the day they became aware of Person A's gambling addiction, or 2 years from the occurrence of the reason. Therefore, Person B must file for divorce within 6 months from the day they became aware of the gambling addiction.

question_eng: What procedures must Persons A, B, and C follow to establish a judicial scrivener corporation, what actions must be taken within two weeks after obtaining establishment approval, and what are the eligibility requirements for members of a judicial scrivener corporation?
answer_eng: To establish a judicial scrivener corporation, Persons A, B, and C must draft the articles of incorporation and obtain approval from the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court through the Seoul Regional Judicial Scrivener Association. question_eng: If an employee, Person A, who is undergoing treatment for an occupational injury, suffers an additional injury due to medical malpractice while receiving treatment at an industrial accident insurance medical institution, can this incident be recognized as an occupational injury?
answer_eng: If Person A, while undergoing treatment for an occupational injury, sustains an additional injury due to medical malpractice during treatment at an industrial accident insurance medical institution, this incident is recognized as an occupational accident under Article 32, Item 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act. Specifically, if the medical malpractice occurred during the treatment process and is closely related to the original occupational injury, and it arose as part of the treatment, it can be recognized as a continued occupational injury.
background_eng: An employee, Person A, working in a manufacturing company, injured their hand on a machine during work and was recognized as having an occupational injury, for which they are currently undergoing treatment. Person A is receiving regular treatment at a designated industrial accident insurance medical institution. Recently, during a procedure at the hospital, Person A suffered a new injury due to medical malpractice. As a result, Person A now has an additional injury on top of the original one and is curious whether this incident can also be recognized as an occupational injury.

contexts.content_eng: If an employee suffers any injury, disease, or disability or dies due to any of the following causes, it shall be deemed an occupational accident: Provided, That this shall not apply where there is no proximate causal relation between his or her duties and the accident: <Amended on Jan. 27, 2010; Oct. 24, 2017; Jan. 15, 2019>1. Accident on duty:(a) Any accident that occurs while he or she performs a duty under his or her employment contract or other acts incidental thereto;(b) Any accident that occurs while he or she uses a facility, etc. provided by his or her business owner, due to any defect in or any careless management of such facility, etc.;(c) Deleted; <Oct. 24, 2017>(d) Any accident that occurs while he or she participates in an event sponsored by or under the direction of his or her business owner or prepares for such event;(e) Any accident that occurs at recess due to an act deemed to be under the control and management of his or her business owner;(f) Any other accident that occurs in connection with his or her duties;2. Occupational disease:(a) Any disease caused by handling or being exposed to any physical agent, chemical substance, dust, pathogen, work imposing a burden on his or her body, or any other agent causing trouble to his or her health while performing his or her duties;(b) Any disease caused by an occupational injury;(c) Any disease caused by work-related mental stress due to workplace harassment, verbal abuse from customers, etc. under Article 76-2 of the Labor Standards Act;(d) Any other disease caused in connection with his or her duties;3. Accident on commuting:(a) Any accident that occurs while he or she commutes to or from work using a transportation means provided by his or her business owner or another similar means under the control and management of his or her business owner;(b) Any accident that occurs while he or she commutes to or from work using other common route and method.

The term "occupational accident" means any injury, disease, disability or death of an employee which is caused by an occupational reason;2. The terms "employee", "wage", "average wage", and "ordinary wage" mean such "employee", "wage", "average wage", and "ordinary wage", respectively as defined in the Labor Standards Act: Provided, That where it is deemed difficult to determine a "wage" or "average wage" pursuant to the Labor Standards Act, the amount determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Employment and Labor shall be the relevant "wage" or "average wage";3. question_eng: If Person A conducts an event similar to the sports promotion voting rights system, offering prizes or financial benefits to those who correctly predict outcomes, and Person B participates in this event for gambling purposes, what penalties do Person A and Person B face, respectively?
answer_eng: Person A, by engaging in activities similar to those regulated under the National Sports Promotion Act, violates Article 26, Paragraph 1 of the Act. question_eng: Person A wishes to purchase Person B's land. In this case, how should the anticipated purchase price be determined, and under what criteria can Person B's land be deemed eligible for purchase?
answer_eng:
The anticipated purchase price should be determined based on the standard market value as prescribed by Article 4 of the Local Tax Act at the time of the purchase request. If there is no standard market value available, the price should be assessed by comparing transaction cases of similar properties within the vicinity.

For Person B's land to be deemed eligible for purchase, it must meet the criteria where the land's utility has diminished due to the inability to use it for its original purpose, or where use and enjoyment are impossible due to legal restrictions. Additionally, there must be no fault attributable to Person B regarding the reduction in utility or the impossibility of use and enjoyment of the land.
background_eng: Person A intends to purchase a parcel of land owned by Person B, located on the outskirts of Seoul. Person B's land has been designated as a river area under the River Act, which has resulted in a reduction of its utility as it can no longer be used for its original purpose. Person A needs to determine the anticipated purchase price for this land, while Person B seeks to confirm whether this land qualifies as a subject for purchase.

contexts.content_eng: The estimated purchase price under Article 80 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "estimated purchase price") shall be the standard market price under Article 4 of the Local Tax Act as at the time such request has been made: Provided, That in cases of absence of the standard market price, it shall be calculated by comparing cases of trade of the relevant item and similar item in a neighboring area. <Amended on Jul. 19, 2016>
contexts.index_eng: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE RIVER ACT / Article. 84 / Procedures for Purchase

contexts.content_eng: Article 85 (Criteria for Determination on Land Subject to Purchase) The criteria for determining land, etc. subject to purchase (hereinafter referred to as "land, etc. subject to purchase") pursuant to Article 79 (1) of the Act shall be as follows. In this regard, the decline in the usefulness of land, etc., or the impossibility of using or benefiting from the land, etc. shall occur through no fault on the part of the requester: <Amended on Jul. 19, 2016>1. Land, etc., the usefulness of which has severely declined because they can no longer be used for their originally intended purposes: They shall be land that can no longer be used according to the category of land use made before the designation of a river area (if the requester proves with official documents that he or she has used the land lawfully for purposes other than the category of land use on the official land register before the designation of the river area, the actual use prior to the designation of a river area shall be deemed the category of land use), buildings thereon, and other fixtures on the land, as at the time the request for purchase has been made;2. Land, etc., the use of or benefit from which is impossible: They shall be land, the use of or benefit from which has become impossible due to the restrictions on activities as required under Articles 33 and 46 of the Act, buildings thereon, and other fixtures on the land.[Title Amended on Jul. 19, 2016]
contexts.index_eng: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE RIVER ACT / Article. 85 / Criteria for Determination on Land Subject to Purchase

question_eng: When can Person A and Person B commence their respective election campaigns, and what is the amount of the deposit required upon candidate registration for each?

question_eng: In the case where Person A and Person B reported false financial information to a public official, resulting in the inclusion of inaccurate facts in the original notarial deed, and used this as the basis for applying for company incorporation registration, how should the registrar handle this application, and what criminal penalties could Person A and Person B face?
answer_eng: The act of Person A and Person B causing inaccurate facts to be recorded in the original notarial deed through false reporting is punishable under Article 228, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Act, with imprisonment for up to five years or a fine of up to 10 million won. Using this in a registration application is punishable under Article 229 of the Criminal Act with the penalty prescribed for the offense. Furthermore, applying for company incorporation registration based on such a falsely created notarial deed falls under the category of "cases where there is a cause for nullity or cancellation of the matters to be registered" according to Article 26, Item 10 of the Commercial Registration Act. Therefore, the registrar must reject the application, providing reasons for the rejection.
background_eng: Person A and Person B agreed to jointly establish a company for the purpose of attracting investment and began preparing the registration procedures for incorporation. Person B proposed to Person A that they exaggerate the company's capital and profit forecasts to appear financially sound and gain the trust of investors, suggesting that they obtain notarization of these exaggerated claims. question_eng: When Person A's friend, Person C, wishes to make a repayment on behalf of Person A, is it legally permissible to do so before the due date, and if Person B refuses, what legal methods are available to offer the repayment?

question_eng: In the event that Person B wishes to file a claim against Person D for the return of the statutory reserved portion, what is the statute of limitations for such a claim, and can the gift made by Person A during his lifetime be included in the calculation of the statutory reserved portion? answer_eng: According to Article 1117 of the Civil Code, Person B must file a claim for the return of the statutory reserved portion within one year from the later of the date of the commencement of the inheritance (March 1, 2022) or the date when Person B became aware of the gift (April 1, 2022). Furthermore, the gift of 100 million won made by Person A to Person D falls within one year prior to the commencement of the inheritance (May 2021) and is thus included in the calculation of the statutory reserved portion pursuant to Article 1114 of the Civil Code. The amount of the statutory reserved portion is calculated by adding the value of Person A's estate at the time of the commencement of the inheritance to the amount of the gift, and then subtracting the total amount of Person A's debts, as stipulated in Article 1113, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Code.

Person A's estate also includes some debts.

question_eng: Under what conditions is the capital gain from the sale of bonds or securities under a repurchase agreement distinguished, and can the income from bonds sold under a repurchase condition be considered interest income? answer_eng: The capital gain from a repurchase agreement refers to the gain from the sale of bonds or securities under a repurchase or resale condition, applying a pre-agreed interest rate according to the repurchase period, as defined in Article 24 of the Enforcement Decree of the Income Tax Act. Additionally, in the case of complex financial products operated by a financial company, where interest-bearing products and derivatives are combined and effectively operated as a single product, the interest income generated from such products is taxed as interest income under Paragraph 5 of the same Article, provided certain conditions are met. These conditions include structural integration or guaranteed returns.
background_eng: Person A is an investment expert affiliated with a financial company, aiming to maximize returns through the use of repurchase agreement (Repo) transactions and complex investment products that combine interest-bearing financial instruments with derivatives in the asset management process. Person A particularly feels the need to distinguish whether the income received from bonds sold under a repurchase condition is capital gains or interest income. Additionally, the company is interested in whether income from products that combine derivatives with interest-generating bonds, under the condition of repurchasing the same bonds after a certain period, is classified as interest income.

question_eng: If Person B does not file an objection to the mediation decision, what legal effect does the mediation decision have? Furthermore, if there was a defect in Person C's litigation capacity, but it was rectified and Person B ratified the decision, does the ratification have retroactive effect?
answer_eng: If Person B does not file an objection to the mediation decision within the prescribed period, pursuant to Article 34, Paragraph 4, Item 1 of the Civil Mediation Act, the mediation decision has the same effect as a judicial settlement. Additionally, even if there was a defect in Person C's litigation capacity, if this defect is subsequently rectified and Person B ratifies the action, according to Articles 60 and 97 of the Civil Procedure Act, the legal action becomes retroactively valid. Therefore, if Person B accepts and ratifies the mediation decision without objection, despite the temporary defect in the legal representative's capacity, the mediation decision is validly confirmed and its effect is retroactive.
background_eng: Person A and Person B agreed to resolve their dispute through a civil mediation process, and the court issued a mediation decision accordingly. However, at the time of mediation, Person B's legal representative, Person C, lacked the necessary documentation to establish proper legal representation due to deficiencies in litigation capacity. Subsequently, the deficiencies regarding Person C's litigation capacity were rectified, and Person B did not file an objection to the mediation decision. After resolving the issue with Person C's qualifications, Person B explicitly ratified the mediation decision.

question_eng: If Person B establishes a severance pay system, what criteria should be used to set it, and how are the average wage and retirement pension systems defined?
answer_eng: When Person B establishes a severance pay system, it must be set up to provide a severance payment of at least 30 days' worth of the average wage for each year of continuous service. The average wage is defined as the total amount of wages paid to the employee during the three months preceding the date on which the reason for calculation arises, divided by the total number of days in that period. Additionally, the retirement pension system includes the defined benefit retirement pension plan, the defined contribution retirement pension plan, and the individual retirement pension plan.

The term "employee" means a person, regardless of the kind of occupation, who offers labor to business or a workplace for the purpose of earning wages;2. The term "work" means both mental work and physical work.4. The term "average wages" means the amount calculated by dividing the total amount of wages paid to a relevant employee during three calendar months immediately before the day grounds for calculating his or her average wages occurred by the total number of calendar days during the three months. The term "contractual work hours" means work hours on which employees and their employer have made an agreement within the limit of work hours under Article 50 or the main clause of Article 69 of this Act, or under Article 139 (1) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act;9. The term "retirement pension plan" means a defined benefit plan, a defined contribution plan, and an individual retirement pension plan;8. The term "defined benefit plan" means a retirement pension plan in which the amount of the benefits an employee will receive is predetermined;9. The term "defined contribution plan" means a retirement pension plan in which the amount of an employer's contribution to pay benefits is predetermined;10. The term "individual retirement pension plan" means a retirement pension plan established to accumulate and operate the lump sum paid by a participant or the contributions paid by an employer or a participant according to the participant's choice in which the amount of the benefits or contributions is not predetermined;11. The term "participant" means an employee who has joined a retirement pension plan or a SME retirement pension fund plan;12. question_eng: If Person A's computer input had resulted in the actual transfer of funds and acquisition of benefits, what punishment could they face? Is it possible to punish Person A even if they did not actually acquire any benefits? When does the statute of limitations begin in this case?

Additionally, since they used this document in an actual real estate transaction, they are also punishable under Article 229 of the Criminal Act with the same penalty. question_eng: In a situation where a single act constitutes both theft and fraud, with a final verdict already rendered for the theft charge and the fraud charge still under trial, what legal effect does a pardon for the fraud charge have on Person A, and what is the overall punishment?
answer_eng:
Person A's act constitutes an ideal concurrence of offenses under Article 40 of the Criminal Code, where a single act constitutes multiple crimes.

Since a final guilty verdict has already been rendered for the theft charge, the court must render a judgment of dismissal for the fraud charge pursuant to Article 326(1) of the Criminal Procedure Act.

Although a special pardon has been granted for the fraud charge, Article 326(2) of the Criminal Procedure Act applies to general pardons and is therefore not applicable in this case.

A final guilty verdict has already been rendered for the theft charge, while the fraud charge is still under trial. During this time, a special pardon was granted for the fraud charge. The issue is how the court should rule on Person A's fraud charge and what the overall punishment should be.

contexts.content_eng: Article 37 (Concurrent Crimes) Several crimes for which judgment has not become final, or a crime for which judgment to punish with an imprisonment without labor or a heavier punishment has become final and the crimes committed before the said final judgment shall be regarded as concurrent crimes. <Amended on Jan. 20, 2004>
contexts.index_eng: CRIMINAL ACT / Article. 37 / Concurrent Crimes

contexts.content_eng: Article 326 (Judgment of Acquittal of Prosecution) Acquittal of a prosecution shall be pronounced by judgment in the following cases:1. Where a finally binding judgment has already been rendered;2. Where amnesty has been proclaimed;3. Where the limitations period has expired;4. Where the punishment has been repealed or the applicable statutes has been amended or abolished subsequent to the commission of the offense.
